title: Eliminating Storage Management Overhead of Deduplication over SSD Arrays Through a Hardware/Software Co-Design
problem: Block-layer deduplication over SSD arrays incurs high storage management overheads in CPU/memory resource usage and I/O performance degradation due to complex dependencies across the storage space.
motivation: Efficient block-level deduplication is critical for storage efficiency, but current implementations impose significant performance penalties that limit practical adoption.
method: ARM-Dedup moves deduplication (finding and removing duplicate data) from the host computer into SSD controllers. Normally, the host's deduplication software maintains one address map while each SSD's internal firmware (the Flash Translation Layer, or FTL) maintains a separate address map, creating redundant work. ARM-Dedup eliminates this by making SSD firmware deduplication-oriented and array-aware—aware of duplicate data and of multiple drives working together—so the SSD controllers handle deduplication storage management directly. The system was built by modifying Linux deduplication software (Dmdedup and mdraid) to work with custom SSD firmware, tested using FEMU SSD emulators.
key_novelty: Making SSD firmware deduplication-oriented and array-aware eliminates the inefficiency of managing array-wide deduplication separately from per-SSD storage management.
contributions: Hardware/software co-design approach that offloads deduplication storage management into SSDs
ARM-Dedup system eliminating redundant dual address mapping between host and FTL layers
Solution addressing array-wide deduplication scope versus per-SSD FTL management mismatch
Prototype achieving up to 272% IOPS improvement in synthetic workloads and 127% in real-world scenarios
primary_theme: Storage deduplication acceleration via hardware/software co-design
